title: La Rocca disputes the letter's dates and band claims
summary: He rejects the letter's dates for Bolden and Clarence Williams, dismisses Johnny Fisher's New York failure, and resents being asked to name other bands.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: I'd like to comment on the dates that she has here to show you she was eaten up, taken in by this communist propaganda. I wish you'd hear this tape recorder. Buddy Bolin, Freddie Kepler, George Pequet left here in 1911. In 1906, by the things that I have in my hand, from Louisiana State Mental Hospital at Jackson, Louisiana, Bolin was incarcerated in there in 1906. He couldn't have played with them. And I've told you when these Negroes came it was 1917. Clarence Williams, he says, left here around 1911 or 13. Clarence Williams would only be 13 years of age. He was still in the country, in Plaquemine, Louisiana. This Negro could be around the age of Armstrong. He could be no more than 58, right now if he's living. Same as Armstrong. And none of them heard Buddy Bolin play. I am going on 70 and I never knew nothing about this Negro Bolin until he's history and started digging from Negro mythology and tales that I don't know where they get him. But did they hear what he played? That's the question. No. They didn't hear what he played. Now they want me to mention Fisher. Now Johnny Fisher brought his band to New York. He was a failure. In his band he played the clarinet. He had George Voth playing the clarinet. He had Happy Shilling playing trombone. And he had several other members that I just don't recall at this present time. And they didn't even secure a job. They tried out all over New York. And they came back on their ears. I don't know whether they rode back the rails or walked home. Now I'm to mention these people. They wouldn't ask Jimmy Durante to mention me that I got him his first jazz band and helped him to put it together. And from that he made his success. They wouldn't ask him that question. But they'll ask me to mention these people who have never made history. This woman must think I was a fool or some other sort of that. Had these men that went before me. If this be true. Then to them I say again would have been the glory. And not to Nick LaRocca's band. That made the success. Sometime later she's supposed to have sent me a letter. Stop that machine.
In this letter. In this letter. In this letter.
